clue.text: Most people get to try Beaujolais Nouveau round the beginning of March

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the single letter from March
Beaujolais Nouveau is the new wine, and 'new' here signals the letters being made into a fresh arrangement
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Most folk will get a chance to sample the new Beaujolais at the start of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nouveau' looks like part of the wine's name, but it is the anagram signal, and 'round' puts the first letter of March inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright majority is more than half the votes or people, which is most of them.

clue.text: Maladie de la guerre

indicators.note: de is French for 'of', so the answer is made of letters from the words la guerre, which hold it

explanation.surface: French for 'disease of the war', the sort of sickness that sweeps through army camps.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written in French: maladie is 'disease' and de is 'of', saying the answer is taken out of la guerre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is an old word for a fever with shivering fits, such as malaria, and maladie is French for illness.

clue.text: Almost see faint light at the end of the tunnel

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

indicators.note: at the end of says take the final letter of each of faint and light

explanation.surface: A hopeful glimmer of light at the far end of a dark tunnel, barely visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light at the end of the tunnel' reads as a stock phrase, but the light and faint only give their last letters, T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger's home is an underground burrow of tunnels, its den or earth.

clue.text: Discombobulated, half intelligible and in the soup?

indicators.note: discombobulated means confused or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
half takes the first six of the twelve letters of intelligible

explanation.surface: Someone confused, only half making sense, and in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' is an idiom for being in trouble, but here it is literal: something found in soup. INTELL, the first half of intelligible, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses such as this small legume are a classic ingredient of thick soups, so it is something found in soup.

clue.text: This measure proposes having fun, swimming where one can

parts.note: to table a motion is to propose it for discussion

indicators.note: having means the pool holds the scrambled letters within it

parts.note: a pool is where one can swim, following on from swimming

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of fun are moving about

explanation.surface: A measure that suggests having fun swimming wherever possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where one can' reads as 'wherever possible' but means the place one can swim; 'swimming' does double duty in the surface only, and here makes NFU from fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoonful of the larger kitchen size is a standard cooking measure of volume.

clue.text: Fox starts to frolic freely in hay?

indicators.note: in places those two letters inside the hay bundle

parts.note: a bale is a bound bundle of hay, the question mark showing it is an example

indicators.note: starts to says take the first letters of frolic and freely

explanation.surface: A fox frolicking freely in a hayfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' looks like the animal, but it is a verb, to puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to puzzle or confuse them, a close synonym of perplex.

clue.text: Delightful and productive drinks party

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the farmland word swallows the party

parts.note: arable land is productive, fit for growing crops
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A lovely, fruitful drinks party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks party' reads as a noun phrase, but 'drinks' is a verb meaning takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is charming and lovable, so it delights.

clue.text: Writer considered trading in Porsche, originally open-topped

parts.note: felt means believed or considered

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of trading, in and Porsche
topped means the first letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A writer thought about part-exchanging his Porsche for a convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open-topped' looks like a car's roof, but it means open with its first letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen with a fibre point is an instrument for writing, so a writer in the tool sense.

clue.text: Be careful playing with seaside toy

indicators.note: playing with means toying with the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A warning to a child to take care while playing with a beach toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom urging someone to go gently and take care.

clue.text: Ridiculous nylon trousers, earrings, necklaces and tops in shocking blue

indicators.note: in places those first letters inside the scrambled colour
shocking suggests the letters are jolted out of order
tops means the first letter of each of nylon, trousers, earrings, necklaces and and

explanation.surface: An outfit of nylon trousers, earrings and necklaces with tops in shocking blue is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking blue' reads as a vivid colour, but 'shocking' is the anagram signal; 'tops' also reaches the word 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position cannot be defended, so it is absurd or ridiculous.

clue.text: Assistant comes up bearing clean copy version for reference

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so in this down entry the assistant sits beneath and carries the rest
a version is a reworked form, so the letters of clean copy are reordered
comes up means rising, so the word reads from the bottom of the down entry upwards

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant brings up a clean copy of a document for reference.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'bearing' means carrying on top: the reversed assistant sits underneath the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-volume book of general knowledge is a standard reference work, consulted for facts.

clue.text: Monsters switching hands and eyes

indicators.note: switching hands means swapping right for left, R and L

parts.note: ogres are monsters of folklore

explanation.surface: Monsters change hands and eyes, like creatures in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes' looks like a noun, but it is a verb, meaning looks at. R and L are right and left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone lecherously, so it means to eye them up.

clue.text: Disappointed Ed — his wench wanted to go topless

indicators.note: to go topless means each of the four words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Ed is let down because his girl wanted to strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word loses its first letter: (e)D (h)IS (w)ENCH (w)ANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disillusioned or let down is a close synonym of disappointed.

clue.text: Folly of cause interrupted by extremely long explanation

indicators.note: interrupted by means the cause word is broken open by the other letters

parts.note: to induce is to cause or bring about

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of long and explanation

explanation.surface: The folly of a cause is interrupted by an overlong explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folly' sounds like a definition of foolishness, and fits loosely: self-indulgence is a kind of folly.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence is giving in to whims or excess, a foolish self-gratification.

clue.text: Exercises can make me ravenous

indicators.note: can make says the letters of me ravenous are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Physical exercise works up a hearty appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercises' looks like a workout, but it means military drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Military manoeuvres are training exercises carried out by troops.

clue.text: Steer straight

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle, of which a steer is an example
a drink taken straight is undiluted, without water or mixer

explanation.surface: An instruction to drive in a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb, but it is a bullock, and neat is an old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit served without ice or mixer is undiluted, and an ox or bullock is old-fashioned cattle.

clue.text: Imitate round dance, finally leads to disaster

indicators.note: round means the imitation word goes around the rest

parts.note: to ape is to imitate

indicators.note: finally leads means the final letter moves to the front

parts.note: calypso is a Caribbean song and dance style

explanation.surface: Copying a round dance is the first step to catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round dance' reads as a kind of dance, but 'round' is the container signal and 'finally leads' brings the dance's last letter to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a catastrophic, world-ending event, a disaster on the grandest scale.

clue.text: Dispatched to cover up gossip that's demanding to be heard

indicators.note: to cover means the dispatched word goes around the reversed gossip

parts.note: dispatched means sent

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the word reads upwards

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

explanation.surface: A person sent to hush up some gossip that people insist on hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' reads as hushing up, but 'up' reverses DIRT to TRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is loud and harsh, so it insists on being heard.

clue.text: Starting up or down round pole, steer away from tradition

indicators.note: round means those first letters go around the pole
starting takes the first letter of up, or and down

parts.note: North is one of the Earth's poles
an ox is a steer, a castrated bull

explanation.surface: Steering up and down round a pole is an odd way to travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb but is the animal, a castrated bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unorthodox departs from the conventional or traditional way.

clue.text: Sometime soon, back home

indicators.note: back says the letters taken from time soon are read in the opposite direction
Some, split off the front of sometime, says only some of the following letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone expects to be home again before long.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sometime' as 'Some time': 'Some' signals that part of time soon is taken, and 'back' turns that part around.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house is a common British home, sharing one wall with its neighbour.

clue.text: Dismisses junction 11 to turn round? Come on!

definitions.meaning: to let go of a worker is to dismiss them
an exclamation urging people to set off

indicators.note: round means the turned letters go around the junction letter
to turn means the letters of 11 across are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 11 across
a T-junction is a road junction shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A sign on a motorway: turn round at junction 11 and get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junction 11' reads as a motorway exit, but 11 points to the 11-across answer, OGLES, rearranged around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing or firing staff is letting them leave, and the phrase is also a rallying call to depart.

clue.text: Group has no right to change sides as paintings in a gallery burn

indicators.note: has no means the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

indicators.note: to change sides means swapping R for L, right for left

parts.note: paintings in a gallery hang in frames

explanation.surface: A group without the right to swap sides watches gallery paintings go up in smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUP loses R to give GOUP; IN FRAMES swaps R for L.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ablaze or burning fiercely is to be consumed by fire.

clue.text: Points raised in public office

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words public office, across the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Issues brought up in a public office.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is a central point, so foci are points of convergence or attention.

clue.text: Girls Aloud drink

indicators.note: aloud says the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Girls Aloud, the British pop group, out for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girls Aloud' reads as the British girl band's name, but is split: Girls is the definition and Aloud the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, traditionally of young women or of birds such as quails.

clue.text: Type of gas that is never right to get promoted

indicators.note: to get promoted means the letter moves up, earlier in the word

explanation.surface: A kind of gas that is never right to be promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: In NEVER, R moves up from the end to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarin and VX belong to a class of chemical weapons named for their effect on the nervous system.

clue.text: At a loose end, but not as loose as a possessor of natural magnetism

indicators.note: but not says some letters are taken away from the fodder before rearranging
loose means the letters are set free into a new order

parts.note: as is read as A's, two letter A

explanation.surface: Being at a loose end, though not as loose as someone with charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not as' reads as a comparison but means 'without A's': the two As go from AT A LOOSE END, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetite is a naturally magnetised mineral, so this stone has magnetism of its own.

clue.text: Substitute queen took her place on the throne last

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

parts.words: took her place on the throne
parts.note: to take one's place on a throne is to sit, past tense sat
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A stand-in queen who ascended the throne last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took her place on the throne' reads as coming to the throne but means sat down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing.

clue.text: See 1
